inputs.content:
# Harlow Fresh Markets: reversing the margin decline — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Harlow Fresh Markets is a family-controlled grocery chain with 58 stores in Ohio and Indiana and a home-delivery
and click-and-collect service launched in 2021. Sales grew from $1.42 billion in FY2023 to $1.50 billion in
FY2025, but operating income fell by more than half.

**Decision maker:** CEO Dana Whitfield, presenting a margin plan to the board in February 2027.

## 2. Decision question

**How should Harlow reverse its declining operating margin, and which actions should it take first?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- **Target:** operating margin back to at least 3.0% by FY2028.
- **Capital:** at most $25M of one-time cost or capital for the plan over FY2026–FY2028.
- **Commitments:** no closure of a store whose lease runs beyond 2027 without a board vote; the family
  owners want to keep the delivery service in some form ("our customers expect it").
- The plan must be credible to the chain's lender: a covenant requires operating income of at least $20M in FY2026.

## 4. Management's current view

The CFO and COO believe **wage inflation is the main cause** of the decline ("the state minimum wage and a tight
labor market have pushed our hourly rate up more than 9% in two years"). Their draft plan: cut scheduled store
labor hours by 8% in FY2026 (they estimate about $14.5M a year of savings) and freeze the e-commerce service at
its current size.

## 5. Financials

**Table 1. Income statement, $ millions (fiscal years end in January)**

|  | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 1,420.0 | 1,468.0 | 1,503.0 |
| Gross profit | 369.8 | 376.0 | 376.1 |
| Store labor | 167.6 | 176.2 | 181.9 |
| Occupancy and energy | 82.4 | 86.6 | 90.2 |
| E-commerce fulfillment (picking + delivery, net of delivery fees) | 5.2 | 10.9 | 18.1 |
| Other SG&A | 66.7 | 69.0 | 70.6 |
| **Operating income** | **47.9** | **33.4** | **15.3** |
| Operating margin | 3.37% | 2.27% | 1.02% |

Gross profit is after shrink (losses from waste, theft and errors). E-commerce sales are included in sales and gross profit.

**Table 2. Gross-margin drivers**

|  | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promotional sales, share of sales | 24.0% | 26.2% | 29.0% |
| Private-label sales, share of sales | 17.0% | 17.7% | 18.5% |
| Shrink, % of sales | 2.1% | 2.3% | 2.6% |

- Promotional sales earn 14 percentage points less gross margin than regular-price sales (unchanged over the period).
- Private-label sales earn 12 percentage points more gross margin than national brands (unchanged).
- Vendor funding covered 55% of promotional markdowns in FY2023 and 46% in FY2025.
- A post-event review of FY2025 promotions found that 38% of events lost money after counting the extra units
  they sold.

## 6. Store labor

**Table 3. Store labor**

|  | FY2023 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Average hourly wage incl. benefits | $16.80 | $18.38 |
| Labor hours per $1,000 of sales | 7.02 | 6.60 |
| Store labor, % of sales | 11.8% | 12.1% |

**Table 4. Shrink by store labor intensity, FY2025 (stores ranked by labor hours per $1,000 of sales)**

| Quartile | Shrink, % of sales |
|---|---|
| Q1 (fewest labor hours per $ sales) | 3.1% |
| Q2 | 2.7% |
| Q3 | 2.4% |
| Q4 (most) | 2.3% |

Shrink composition FY2025: fresh and produce waste 45%, theft 35%, administrative and receiving errors 20%.
Store managers in the lowest-labor quartile say produce rotation and receiving checks are skipped on busy days.

## 7. E-commerce

**Table 5. E-commerce operating data**

|  | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-commerce share of sales | 3.0% | 5.6% | 8.5% |
| Orders, thousands | 453 | 865 | 1,331 |
| Average basket | $94 | $95 | $96 |
| Share of orders delivered to the home (rest: click-and-collect) | 45% | 52% | 58% |
| Picking cost per order (all orders) | $7.20 | $7.30 | $7.40 |
| Third-party delivery cost per delivered order | $12.90 | $13.40 | $13.80 |
| Average delivery fee collected per delivered order | $3.40 | $3.20 | $3.10 |

- Delivery is free above $75 (a $4.99 fee below). Click-and-collect is free.
- Survey of 2,300 e-commerce customers (FY2025): 70% of what they buy online they say they would otherwise have
  bought in a Harlow store.
- Finance estimates that a dollar of sales that is genuinely new to Harlow adds about 20 cents of contribution
  (gross margin less variable store costs), before e-commerce fulfillment.
- **Fee test** (4 stores, 10 weeks, late FY2025): delivery fee raised to $7.99 and the free-delivery threshold to
  $100. Delivered orders fell 9%, click-and-collect orders rose 14%, total e-commerce sales fell 2%, and the
  average fee collected per delivered order rose to $6.40.

## 8. Store portfolio

**Table 6. The nine weakest stores, FY2025**

|  | Value |
|---|---|
| Stores with negative four-wall EBITDA | 9 of 58 |
| Their combined sales | $118.0M |
| Their combined four-wall EBITDA | −$3.1M |
| Leases expiring by end of 2027 | 6 of the 9 |
| Estimated lease-exit cost for the other 3 | $7.5M (one-time) |
| Share of their sales expected to move to a nearby Harlow store if closed (past closures) | 25% |
| Contribution on sales moved to a receiving store | 12% |

## 9. Customers and competitors

- A discount grocer, ValuMart, has opened 11 stores in Harlow trade areas since 2023. Harlow stores within three
  miles of a new ValuMart had comparable sales of −4.2% in FY2025, against +1.1% for other Harlow stores.
- Customer survey (n = 3,100): 41% say Harlow is "more expensive than other options" (FY2023: 33%); top reasons
  to shop Harlow are fresh produce (58%) and convenience (44%).
- Category managers say they raised promotional depth in FY2024–FY2025 "to defend traffic against ValuMart".

## 10. Other material circulated to the board

- **E-commerce team update:** "E-commerce is profitable: a contribution margin of 6.1% of e-commerce sales in FY2025."
  Their calculation takes the gross margin on all e-commerce sales and deducts picking, packaging and an allocation
  of store variable costs. Third-party delivery is not in it (finance books it in "E-commerce fulfillment"), and it
  treats every e-commerce sale as new to Harlow.
- **Category team:** "Stores with the deepest promotions in FY2025 grew comparable sales 1.8%, against 0.2% for the
  rest. Promotions work."

## 11. Uncertainties

- How much of the promotional increase is needed to hold traffic against ValuMart.
- Whether third-party delivery rates can be renegotiated (contract renews in 2026; the provider proposed a 3% rise).
- Wage rates: the state minimum wage rises again in 2027 (+4%).
- How customers would respond to labor-hour cuts (checkout waits, stock-outs).

storyline.governing_thought: Fix promotions, shrink and delivery pricing before cutting hours; with store exits, margin reaches 2.5% by FY2028, 3.0% with targeted hours

exec_summary.text: Margin fell 2.35 percentage points in two years, mostly in gross margin and e-commerce, not wages

sub_points.text: Gross margin and e-commerce explain 79% of it; labor 13%
Promotions and shrink cost $18M of FY2025 gross profit

exec_summary.text: Promotions and shrink are the biggest fix: a promotion reset adds $9.9M a year; hour cuts raise shrink

sub_points.text: Promotions hit 29% of sales, yet 41% call Harlow expensive
ValuMart's pressure is local; chain-wide promotions do not pay

exec_summary.text: E-commerce and nine weak stores lose $13.5M a year; delivery pricing and store exits recover $9.1M

sub_points.text: Counted in full, e-commerce loses $10.4M a year
The tested delivery fee cuts that loss by $2.5M

exec_summary.text: No-capital moves first protect the covenant; the plan reaches 2.5% by FY2028, 3.0% with targeted hours

sub_points.text: The 2027 wage rise cuts FY2028 margin from 3.0% to 2.5%
Management's hours cut leaves FY2028 margin at 1.0–1.5%

next_steps.action: Approve the plan, the three store-exit votes and the $7.5M lease-exit budget
Drop money-losing promotion events and reopen vendor-funding terms
Stop the 8% hours cut; restore produce rotation and receiving checks in the leanest stores
Roll out the tested delivery fee and negotiate the carrier renewal
Track the covenant monthly; bring a targeted hours plan to the FY2027 gate

constraints.item: Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028
constraints.effect: the base case reaches about 2.5% after the 2027 wage rise; the governing thought, exec item 4 and the bridge title say 3.0% needs targeted hours
taken in full in the FY2028 bridge, about $6.85M

constraints.item: Carrier's proposed 3% rate rise at the 2026 renewal (known cost)
constraints.effect: taken in the FY2026 and FY2028 estimates, about $0.29M

constraints.item: Covenant: operating income of at least $20M in FY2026
constraints.effect: first-wave estimate of $25.2M; holds if at least 49% of the first wave lands

constraints.item: At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028
constraints.effect: only quantified cost is the $7.5M lease exit; closure costs for the six lapsing leases are not in the pack and flagged

constraints.item: No closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote
constraints.effect: three of the nine exits are put to the board; next steps ask for the vote

constraints.item: Owners want to keep delivery in some form

alternatives.option: Management's draft: cut store hours 8% in FY2026 and freeze e-commerce
alternatives.why: it clears the covenant fastest, but shrink and the wage rise erase its saving by FY2028 and leave margin at 1.0–1.5%; a smaller, targeted cut in the most-staffed stores is kept as the lever that closes the gap to 3.0%

alternatives.option: Keep promotion depth to defend traffic against ValuMart (category team)
alternatives.why: ValuMart's effect is local and the deep-promotion comp gain pays for only 2.3 percentage points of promo share

alternatives.option: Exit only the six stores whose leases lapse, avoiding the $7.5M and the board vote
alternatives.why: it saves $7.5M but gives up about $2.2M a year that the plan needs; payback about 3.4 years
ruled out by the owners' commitment; the pack has no data on how delivered customers would react

failure_threshold.driver: how far promotional share comes back down
failure_threshold.threshold: each percentage point left in place costs about $2.0M; even with no promotion reset at all the plan stays above management's 1.5% best case. The FY2026 covenant breaks if less than 49% of the first wave lands
failure_threshold.range: FY2028 margin 2.2% low (promotions back only to FY2024's 26.2%) / 2.5% base / 2.7% high (shrink back to FY2023's 2.1%, carrier rate flat)

consistency.headline: Fix promotions, shrink and delivery pricing before cutting hours; with store exits, margin reaches 2.5% by FY2028, 3.0% with targeted hours
consistency.fix: headline changed from 'reaches 3.0%' to 'about 2.5%, 3.0% with targeted hours' once the 2027 wage rise was included
